newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary wheat prices dive in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Hungary wheat prices dive in brisk trade.

text.p: Grain futures extended their decline on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Tuesday, with March milling wheat plummeting 1,170 forints per tonne as excess stocks continued to make their impact, traders said.
"There was continuous trade at this level and a relatively high turnover," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
March milling wheat was exempt from the daily 400 forint limit on price movements.
Under BCE rules, if a maturity drops five consecutive days by the daily allowed maximum of 400 forints, the limit is then removed until the daily decline again becomes smaller than 400 forints.
March milling wheat ended at 25,840 forints.
Herczeg said it could fall further. "The fact that the May maturity dropped by the limit could indicate further drops for March as well," he said.
The BCE said other positions were just one day away from free-fall.

"The limit on May, August, September, October and December milling wheat as well as December feed maize would also be removed if the limit-down drop continues on Wednesday," said BCE spokesman Peter Janoska.
Traders were not surprised by the drop, with surplus maize and wheat expected to appear on the market as producers sought to finance spring farm work.
"Sellers have appeared with sizeable volumes on offer, probably realising their earlier expectations (of higher prices) were wrong," Herczeg said.
Turnover was a solid 2,287 contracts, or 899.67 million forints, of which maize accounted for 1,395 contracts and milling wheat for 686.
Lot size is 20,000 kg for all contracts.
